overview.description: Manni (meaning 'little man' or 'chap') is the national card game of Iceland, played with three players and a 48-card deck. The game features a unique 'Manni' - a spare hand of four cards dealt to the table that the declarer can use to improve their hand. With four different contracts (Grand, Spades, Other, and Nullo), players must play each contract once during the 12-deal game.
overview.deck: 52-card pack (Trjámann: 16 each, 4 to Manni). Basic Manni uses 48 cards (twos removed), 12 each, 12 Manni.

history.origins: Manni is the national card game of Iceland, with numerous local variations across the country. The name refers to the spare hand (Manni) that can be used to improve a player's hand.

setup.players: 3 players. Each plays individually in some contracts; in others, the declarer plays against the other two.

rules.objective: Score the highest net positive points after 12 deals by making or breaking contract targets.
rules.gameplay: Standard trick-taking rules apply. Must follow suit if possible. If void, may play any card. Trump suit wins over plain suits. Highest card of led suit wins if no trumps.
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible; if void may play any card.
Trick won by highest trump if any, else highest card of led suit. Winner leads next trick.
Declarer (left of dealer) chooses contract: Grand, Spades, Other, or Nullo. Each player must play each contract once over 12 deals.
Declarer may discard up to 4 cards and draw from the Manni before play.

strategy.basic: Use the Manni exchange wisely - discard weak cards and hope to draw trumps or high cards. In Nullo, get rid of high cards early by playing them when you can't win the trick.
strategy.intermediate: Card counting is essential. Track which high cards have been played, especially in Nullo where you want to avoid taking tricks. In Grand and suit contracts, estimate how many tricks you can realistically win.
strategy.advanced: Contract selection strategy: Choose Grand when you have balanced high cards across suits. Choose a suit contract when you have length and strength in that suit. Choose Nullo when you have low cards and short suits. The exchange decision: Sometimes keeping a moderately strong hand is better than risking the Manni.
tips: In Nullo, leading low cards in long suits often forces opponents to win tricks they don't want
Remember that in the 3-player game, there are only 16 tricks total
Track which Aces and Kings have been played - they determine who will win subsequent tricks
In suit contracts, voiding yourself in a weak suit lets you trump when that suit is led

list.name: Basic Manni
list.description: 48 cards (twos removed), 12 each, 12 to Manni. Trump rotates hearts, spades, diamonds, clubs. Player to dealer's left may exchange all 12 cards with Manni. Score: +1 per trick over 4; first to 10 points wins.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation uses same engine; deal and scoring differ as described above.

list.name: Trjámann
list.description: Full 52-card pack, 16 each, 4 to Manni. Declarer (left of dealer) chooses contract: Nullo, Grand, Spades, or Other. Declarer may discard up to 4 and draw from Manni. 12 deals; each player must play each contract once. Targets: 8/4/4 (Grand/Spades/Other) or 4/6/6 (Nullo).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation uses same engine; contract choice and targets as described.

list.name: Hornafjarðarmanni
list.description: 52 cards with twos. Deal: 4 to Manni, then 3 to each, repeated until Manni has 16 and each player 12. Cut card determines contract (ten+ no trump, 6-9 suit trump, 5 or lower nóló). Left of dealer may discard up to 7 and replace from Manni; right up to 5; dealer the rest. First to 10 positive points ends game; net score decides winner.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation uses same engine; deal pattern and contract determination differ.

list.name: Laugavatnsmanni
list.description: Similar to Trjámann with six contracts (Nullo, Grand, Spades, Hearts, Clubs, Diamonds), 18 deals. Bidding: left of dealer chooses contract; others may take over with a 'great' contract (14 tricks for declarer, 1 each for opponents). Great contract outbid by denomination: Grand highest, then hearts, spades, diamonds, clubs.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation uses same engine; contracts and bidding as described.
